title: Neurodynamic Assessment and Treatment
lead: Nerves must glide and lengthen as we move.

blocks.text: Nerves must glide and lengthen as we move. A sensitised nerve (for example after root irritation or entrapment) responds to movement with pain or paraesthesia. Neurodynamic tests load the nervous system in sequence; **structural** **differentiation** (changing a distant body part that moves the nerve but not the local muscle) helps decide whether symptoms come from neural tissue.

blocks.label: TEACHER'S VOICE
body: A neurodynamic test is "positive" only if it reproduces the patient's familiar symptoms and the response changes with structural differentiation. A stretch feeling in the hamstrings is not a positive SLR.

rows: Add ankle dorsiflexion or neck flexion; symptom change suggests neural
Sitting slump, neck flexion, knee extension, ankle dorsiflexion
Release neck flexion: symptom reduction suggests neural
Shoulder depression, abduction 110°, wrist and finger extension, forearm supination, shoulder lateral rotation, elbow extension
Neck side flexion away increases, toward decreases
Shoulder depression, elbow extension, internal rotation, forearm pronation, wrist and finger flexion
Wrist and finger extension, forearm pronation, elbow flexion, shoulder depression and abduction
Lengthens the nerve bed at one end while shortening it at the other (for example neck extension with knee extension in slump)
Treat the surrounding tissues (joint mobilisation, posture)
When compression is the main issue

blocks.text: Dose: 10 slow, smooth repetitions, 2 to 3 times per day, without symptom flare lasting more than a few minutes.

items: **What makes a neurodynamic test positive?** Familiar symptoms reproduced and changed by structural differentiation.
**Which technique for an irritable nerve?** Sliders.
**Name the ULNT for the median nerve.** ULNT1.
**What should happen after a neural mobilisation session?** No lasting flare; any increase should settle quickly.
**Hamstring stretch only on SLR, unchanged by dorsiflexion?** Likely muscle, not neural.

sections.title: Now You Should Be Able To

items: Perform neurodynamic tests with structural differentiation.
Choose sliders or tensioners by irritability.
